newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain invites Israel, PLO to mark peace-separately.
newsitem.headline: Spain invites Israel, PLO to mark peace-separately.

text.p: Spain has asked Israeli and Palestinian leaders to come to Madrid to commemorate a historic peace conference five years ago but has issued separate invitations, reflecting the resurgent tensions in the region.
The Spanish Foreign Ministry confirmed on Friday it had issued separate invitations to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to visit on or around October 31.
On that date five years ago, a landmark conference in Madrid brought Israel, Syria, Jordan and Palestinians to the negotiating table after more than four decades of war.
"The occasion of the fifth anniversary of the Madrid peace conference reminded Spanish authorities of the peace process," said a Foreign Ministry official who asked not to be identified.
Spain did not intend it as a multilateral meeting or a second Madrid conference, the official said.
Arafat has accepted the offer but no date has been set, the ministry said.
The Israeli embassy in Madrid said Netanyahu has not yet responded.
"Arafat has said he will come. It will be a bilateral visit," the official said. "It is just a way for the Spanish government to express its concern."
Israeli embassy spokesman Ofer Bavly said he did not know of any ceremonies planned for the commemoration.
"It looks like they are inviting them on separate dates and we haven't seen them inviting anyone else," he told Reuters.
The low-key anniversary underlines deep tensions in the region after a burst of violence killed more than 70 Arabs and Israelis last month.
The renewal of clashes last month over Israel's opening of an archaeological tunnel in Jerusalem posed the biggest crisis in the peace effort since it was lauched.
Diplomatic sources in Madrid viewed the invitation as part of an effort by the European Union to reassert itself in the flailing Mideast peace process.
"The EU is trying to play a bigger role in the Middle East peace process. That would be part of this effort," said one diplomat who asked not to be named.
"The overall strategy is to reassert the European position and to reassert Spain's role. They (Spain) are vying for attention in Europe," the diplomat said.
Some Arab leaders have called on Europe to get more involved in the peace process to balance what they view as a U.S. bias toward Israel.
However, Israel has made clear it considers the United States the only acceptable broker for peace talks.

In recent years, Spain has carved out a niche as a bridge between Europe and non-European Mediterranean countries. In November 1995, it hosted a European-Mediterranean conference in Barcelona which Israelis and Arabs also attended.
